# OpenAPI read/write, SDK and CLI calls

> Current data contract data/3: Collection-scoped Record actions and /uns/records:transact replace duplicate data routes. Samples use samples:find/aggregate/latest/delete; append to /records/{recordId}/samples. Find/aggregate require from/to and support multiple optional recordIds; latest/delete require explicit recordIds. Find and write snapshots share canonical resource objects with business fields under data; query paths remain bare business fields and _id/_meta.*. See the [data contract](tier0://mcp/skill-docs/doc/uns-v2/data-api.md).

MCP defaults to reading; writes/deletes require explicit consent and a dryRun preview. Contract and example tools expose the current UNS schemas and curl/SDK/CLI requests. Instance URLs, IDs and keys remain placeholders.

Internal /api/core/v2 and OpenAPI /openapi/v2 share suffixes and contracts. Record uses Collection-scoped document actions; Sample append uses items arrays and /uns/records:transact composes business steps and metadata:transact composes metadata. Optional idempotencyKey and expectedRevision; supplied keys deduplicate retries and supplied revisions enforce concurrency checks. Query accepted jobId with jobs/query. After a timeout inspect business state before submitting again. Configuration saving is not deployment or ingestion.

## Existing TypeScript SDK

The public `@tier0/sdk` configureClient/getClient().post surface was checked against version 0.2.8. Existing v1 convenience methods remain; use the generic client for UNS v2 rather than inventing generated methods:

```typescript
import { configureClient, getClient } from '@tier0/sdk';
configureClient({ apiHost: '<INSTANCE_BASE_URL>', apiKey: '<API_KEY>' });
const result = await getClient().post('/openapi/v2/uns/collections/<COLLECTION_ID>/records:find', {
  filter: {}, limit: 20
});
```

## Existing CLI

```bash
tier0 login --base-url <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>
tier0 api /openapi/v2/uns/collections/<COLLECTION_ID>/records:find --body-file records-query.json --json
```

Use the same request JSON in records-query.json. Existing SDK/CLI authentication paths are preserved.

## App data APIs

An App-bound data key uses `/openapi/v2/uns/apps/context` with `{}` to discover its granted Collections; a request appId cannot impersonate that identity. Platform credential management uses `/openapi/v2/uns/apps/keys/create` with appId/name and `/openapi/v2/uns/apps/keys/revoke` with appId/keyId, requiring the existing App credential-management permission. MCP documentation tools can describe these contracts and SDK/CLI examples, but there is no corresponding MCP execution tool and MCP does not return actual keys.
